cards.title: Assessing Disease-State and Study Differences Before Transferring Animal PK
cards.claim: When PK estimates differ across disease models or studies, retain infection or disease state, severity, route, dose range, body size and study design as potential explanations. A cross-study contrast does not isolate the causal effect of disease or establish a universal direction of clearance change.
conditions: Animal PK data are compared across disease states, strains or study designs.
Parameter definitions and absolute versus body-weight-normalized units are made comparable first.
required_inputs: Study-specific concentration-time data or qualified parameter estimates with uncertainty.
Disease-state and severity descriptors, biological population, dosing route/range and body weight.
Model structure, assay method and sampling design for each study.
limitations: Study-level confounding prevents attributing all differences to one physiological cause.
Do not transfer a clearance multiplier or disease effect from another analyte.
cards.downstream_use: Decide whether a PK source is applicable to the intended PD model and whether matched PK data or an explicit sensitivity scenario is needed.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
